name: Diabetic, Hypertensive and Vascular Retinal Disease

reference.source: Parsons' Diseases of the Eye 23rd Edition (topic map; text rewritten, no verbatim copy)
clinicalPearls: Disc swelling with hypertension is malignant
Ischaemic vein disease grows iris vessels
Cherry spot means blocked artery: hurry
reference.pathophysiology: Pericyte loss balloons capillaries into microaneurysms leaking lipid while VEGF sprouts fragile new vessels that bleed and fibrose; hypertensive medial hyperplasia narrows lumens compressing veins at crossings, and embolic or arteritic occlusion infarcts inner retina leaving choroidal foveal blush.
additionalDifferentials: Proliferative versus maculopathy by vessels versus thickness
Ischaemic versus nonischaemic vein occlusion by vision and RAPD
Artery versus vein occlusion by pallor versus blood
additionalInvestigations: Fluorescein angiography for ischaemia and leak
Carotid, cardiac and arteritis workup in arterial events
